extraction.name: FLORES-101 Evaluation Benchmark for Low-Resource and Multilingual Machine Translation
extraction.description: An evaluation benchmark consisting of 3001 sentences extracted from English Wikipedia and translated into 101 languages by professional translators. It is designed for low-resource and multilingual machine translation evaluation, including many-to-many translation, document-level evaluation, and multimodal evaluation via rich metadata.
extraction.creator: Naman Goyal, Cynthia Gao, Vishrav Chaudhary, Peng-Jen Chen, Guillaume Wenzek, Da Ju, Sanjana Krishnan, Marc’Aurelio Ranzato, Francisco Guzmán, Angela Fan
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Sentences were extracted from English Wikipedia sources, with one article selected at random from each source domain and a few contiguous sentences manually selected from each article. The selected sentences were then translated into 101 languages by professional translators through a controlled translation workflow with automatic checks and human evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping, Others
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper notes that some languages were considered but were unable to meet the quality bar after rounds of re-translation; it does not describe item-level missing data in the released benchmark.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Multiple Wikimedia sources, specifically English Wikipedia, including Wikinews, Wikijunior, and WikiVoyage articles.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Sentences were manually selected from articles, avoiding very short or malformed sentences; one paragraph per document was selected from the beginning, middle, or end to balance document position. Translations underwent automatic checks and, if needed, re-translation and minimal editing.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Very short or malformed sentences were avoided during selection. Automatic quality checks filtered translations for language identification, copying of the source, abnormal length, fluency, and similarity to commercial translation engines; translations failing checks were re-translated before human evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: 10 annotators in the lab manually selected sentences and labeled each sentence with one of 10 sub-topics. Professional translators translated the sentences, and independent evaluation LSPs assessed translation quality using a 0-100 Translation Quality Score based on error categories including grammar, punctuation, spelling, capitalization, addition/omission, mistranslation, unnatural translation, untranslated text, and register. Translations below threshold were re-translated.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Translation quality was scored per language on a 0 to 100 scale using error counts and severity levels (minor, major, critical). The acceptable threshold was set to 90%. The paper also reports that automatic checks were used to detect likely copies from translation engines and that some languages required re-translation.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: For sentence selection, 10 annotators in the lab: 6 male and 4 female; roles included researchers (scientists and engineers) and program/project managers; they came from East Asia, South Asia, Southern Europe, Latin America, and North America.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Language identification, length checking, language-model fluency checking, SentencePiece BLEU (spBLEU), and heuristics comparing translations to outputs from publicly available translation engines; clustering techniques were used to determine cutoff values for copy detection.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dev and devtest splits are publicly downloadable; the test set is not released and is available only through a public evaluation server. The paper states an intention to continue expanding the number of languages and to make the test set available via community evaluation efforts, but no formal versioning or deprecation policy is given.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Gender, region of origin, and professional role of annotators are explicitly described. The dataset metadata also includes language, script, language family, and resource level for the translated languages.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to foster progress in low-resource and multilingual machine translation and to support evaluation beyond MT, including document-level translation, multimodal translation, sentence/document classification, language identification, and multilingual domain adaptation.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes potential translationese effects because source sentences are translated from English into other languages. It also discusses that low-resource languages may be more susceptible to translator variance and that automatic engine-copy bias had to be actively mitigated.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Coverage is limited to 3001 sentences and 101 languages. Source sentences come only from English Wikipedia and three domains, so domain coverage is broad but not exhaustive. The paper notes that translationese may affect evaluation, that some languages could not meet the quality bar, and that performance varies strongly with resource level and language family.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation benchmark for many-to-many multilingual machine translation; dev for hyper-parameter tuning; devtest for testing during development; test for evaluation via server; also intended for document-level translation, multimodal translation, sentence/document classification, language identification, and multilingual domain adaptation.
